# IBRA

Hebrew spelling and pronunciation: איברה (ee-BRA).

> The problem IBRA solves: people train at home, sometimes for years, and don't see real change in their body. IBRA builds a plan for the equipment the user already owns, runs it set by set, measures the body (shoulders, waist, photos, posture) and progresses the plan every week. Free for every man. IBRA Pro connects the user's own AI chat (ChatGPT, Claude or Gemini), which also sees the progress photos and fine-tunes the plan weekly. Workouts of about 30–40 minutes.
>
> IBRA is an iPhone app (Hebrew and English); Android (Google Play) is coming soon. It has a daily player for sets, rest and meals, body measurements and photos, and a weekly close that progresses the plan (and, in Pro, sends what really happened to the chat for adjustments). Training needs no account and no server; data stays on the phone and in the user's iCloud. The one exception is the optional squad: what you share with friends is stored on IBRA's server (Supabase, EU) so they can see it. One free sample day without signing up. Pricing: the core app is free with no AI required (IBRA builds the first plan from your equipment and goal, runs it and progresses it at each weekly close). IBRA Pro connects your own AI chat as a coach, plus photo analysis, body fat, posture, charts and the Apple Watch app: ₪249.90/year or ₪49.90/month; the first close with the coach is free. The AI chat is billed separately by its provider. Cancelling never locks data. Ranks: בֶּן חַיִל (Son of Valor) is free; אִישׁ חַיִל and גִּבּוֹר חַיִל are in Pro.
>
> Sick or wiped out: the morning routine has "Feeling off?". Pick Sick or Worn out and the app pauses workouts, keeps the routine, sleep and food, and asks about your energy each day. After four days or more off, the first three weighted workouts come back gradually: 85%, 90%, 95% of the load, then full.
